title: AdaptiveRethink: Dynamic Reflection Depth Control for Vision-Language Models via Difficulty-Aware Reinforcement Learning
description:
Problem: VL-Rethinker's Forced Rethinking uniformly appends a single rethinking trigger regardless of problem difficulty, wasting computation on simple problems while potentially under-reflecting on highly complex ones. Optimal reasoning depth should be conditioned on problem difficulty.

Proposed Method: We introduce AdaptiveRethink, which learns a difficulty-aware reflection policy jointly with the reasoning policy. Concretely, we augment GRPO with a secondary reward signal that penalizes unnecessary rethinking steps on easy problems (measured by reward variance across rollouts as a proxy for difficulty) and rewards deeper multi-turn reflection on hard problems. We parameterize reflection depth as a discrete latent variable (0, 1, 2, or 3 rethinking triggers) and train the model to select depth dynamically. We also incorporate a computational budget penalty term scaled inversely with problem difficulty to incentivize efficiency.

Experiments: (1) Compare against VL-Rethinker and fixed-depth baselines on MathVista, MathVerse, MathVision, MMMU-Pro across accuracy and average token count; (2) Ablate the difficulty proxy (reward variance vs. ground-truth difficulty labels); (3) Analyze depth selection distributions stratified by problem difficulty level; (4) Evaluate generalization to out-of-domain visual reasoning benchmarks (ScienceQA, ChartQA) to test whether adaptive depth transfers beyond math domains.

title: AdaptiveRethink: Learning When to Reflect via Meta-Reinforcement Learning for Vision-Language Models
description:

Proposed Method: We introduce a lightweight difficulty-aware gating mechanism trained via meta-reinforcement learning. Concretely, we augment the base VLM with a small 'reflection controller' that, after an initial fast-thinking rollout, predicts whether rethinking will improve accuracy. The controller is trained end-to-end with a modified GRPO reward that penalizes unnecessary rethinking (tokens used × reflection frequency) while rewarding correctness gains. SSR is retained to handle vanishing advantages.

description:

A model that learns *when* to trigger self-reflection—rather than always doing so—would be more efficient and potentially more accurate. Proposed Method: We introduce a lightweight 'reflection gating' mechanism trained via meta-RL. Alongside the primary VLM, we train a small policy head that observes the model's initial rollout (e.g., confidence signals, answer consistency across partial rollouts, problem complexity embeddings) and decides whether to append the rethinking trigger. We use a two-stage GRPO training: Stage 1 trains the base VLM with SSR as in VL-Rethinker; Stage 2 jointly fine-tunes the gate policy using a reward signal that balances final answer correctness against token-budget cost (penalizing unnecessary reflections). The gate is trained with a separate advantage estimator comparing reflection vs. no-reflection trajectories. Planned Experiments: Evaluate on MathVista, MathVerse, MathVision, MMMU-Pro comparing (1) baseline VLM, (2) VL-Rethinker with forced rethinking, (3) AdaptiveRethink. Metrics include accuracy, average token length per problem, and accuracy-vs-compute Pareto curves. We also analyze gate decisions qualitatively to validate they correlate with human-judged problem difficulty.

title: AdaptiveRethink: Learning When to Reflect in Vision-Language Models via Meta-Reinforcement Learning
description:
Problem: VL-Rethinker's Forced Rethinking unconditionally triggers self-reflection after every rollout, which wastes compute on easy problems and may introduce noise by forcing reflection where it adds no value. A key open question is: can a model learn *when* reflection is genuinely beneficial rather than always reflecting?

Proposed Method: We introduce a meta-RL framework where the VLM learns a reflection gating policy alongside its reasoning policy. Concretely, we augment GRPO with a lightweight binary gate module that predicts, after an initial answer rollout, whether a rethinking pass is warranted. The gate is trained end-to-end using a composite reward: (1) correctness reward from the final answer, and (2) an efficiency penalty proportional to total token length when the gate triggers unnecessary reflection (i.e., reflection that doesn't improve the answer). Selective Sample Replay (SSR) is retained to handle vanishing advantages. The gate learns to activate reflection selectively — primarily on hard, uncertain, or visually ambiguous problems.

Experiments: (1) Accuracy vs. compute trade-off on MathVista, MathVerse, MathVision comparing always-reflect, never-reflect, and adaptive baselines; (2) Analysis of gate activation patterns across difficulty levels; (3) Ablation of the efficiency penalty coefficient; (4) Generalization to science/chart QA benchmarks (MMMU-Pro, EMMA). We hypothesize adaptive reflection matches forced-rethinking accuracy while reducing inference FLOPs by 30-40% on easy problem subsets.

title: AdaptiveRethink: Learning When to Reflect via Meta-Reinforcement Learning for Vision-Language Models
description:
Problem: VL-Rethinker's Forced Rethinking applies self-reflection unconditionally to all problems, wasting compute on trivial questions while potentially providing insufficient reflection depth for highly complex ones. An ideal slow-thinking model should dynamically allocate reflection effort based on problem difficulty and uncertainty.

Proposed Method: We introduce AdaptiveRethink, a meta-RL framework that trains a lightweight 'reflection controller' jointly with the VLM reasoner. The controller learns a difficulty-aware policy that decides: (1) whether to trigger reflection at all, (2) how many reflection iterations to perform (1-3), and (3) when to terminate rethinking early if confidence is sufficient. We formalize this as a two-level RL problem: the outer level optimizes reflection allocation using a reward that balances accuracy gain against token cost (efficiency-adjusted reward), while the inner level uses GRPO with SSR for reasoning quality. The controller receives as input the model's intermediate hidden states and predicted answer entropy as uncertainty signals.

Experiments: We evaluate on MathVista, MathVerse, MathVision, and MMMU-Pro, measuring both accuracy and average token usage. Ablations compare fixed 0/1/2/3-reflection baselines against adaptive allocation. We analyze correlation between controller decisions and problem difficulty ratings. Expected outcome: matching or exceeding VL-Rethinker accuracy with 30-40% fewer reflection tokens on average.

title: Adaptive Rethinking Depth: Learning When and How Much to Reflect in Vision-Language Reasoning
description:
Problem: VL-Rethinker's Forced Rethinking applies a uniform rethinking trigger regardless of question difficulty or model confidence, potentially wasting computation on easy problems while under-investing reflection on genuinely hard ones. An ideal slow-thinking VLM should dynamically calibrate reflection depth based on problem complexity and intermediate confidence signals.

Proposed Method: We introduce Adaptive Rethinking Depth (ARD), which augments RL training with a learned 'reflection gating' mechanism. During GRPO rollouts, we train a lightweight confidence estimator (a shallow MLP head on the VLM's hidden states) that predicts answer reliability after each reasoning step. This confidence score gates whether to trigger 0, 1, or multiple rethinking rounds via a discrete action in the RL reward formulation. The reward combines task accuracy with a computation cost penalty proportional to reflection depth, creating a Pareto-optimal trade-off. We use SSR from VL-Rethinker to handle vanishing advantages across this extended action space.

Experiments: (1) Accuracy vs. inference FLOPs curves on MathVista, MathVerse, MathVision, and MMMU-Pro compared to fixed-depth baselines; (2) Difficulty stratification analysis showing reflection depth correlates with problem hardness; (3) Ablations on cost penalty weight; (4) Human evaluation of reflection quality across depth levels.
